issues.issue: First numbered Book III Chapter XCVIII is sequential research editorial XCIX, following 98 earlier indexed numbered chapters; preserve printed/editorial labels.
The chapter begins on PDF534/printed500 with a merchant natal horoscope and ends above printed Animodar CHAP XCIX divider on PDF539/printed505.
The birth figure appears dated 19 September 1616 with a PM time and latitude 53°, but exact minute glyphs and true observer's location remain unverified.
The merchant is not an identified independent individual; birth certificate, later life accidents and contemporaneous forecast records are absent.
Lilly defines the birth instant as infant separation and first breath, historically not guaranteed to coincide with modern clinical recorded birth time.
Trutine of Hermes birth and conception Moon/Ascendant reciprocity is a historical claim, not a proven astronomical cause of timing of human childbirth.
The conception Moon or its opposite sign allowed at birth widens the rule's matching range.
Lilly explicitly says exact rising degree consistency within one to three degrees often fails, though he sometimes recovers the rising sign after hour-level birth-time errors.
Success in guessing a sign is a different endpoint from reconstructing recorded birth time to the minute or rising degree.
His citations to Ptolemy's Centiloquium aphorism 51, Schoner, Pontanus, Junctinus and Heydon are appeals to tradition and require separate textual/historical authentication.
Charts rectified 'by Accidents' are described as external confirmation for Trutine; this may be circular if the accident method itself determines the correct ascendant.
His gestation table uses Moon-above-versus-below-horizon and angular distances from ascendant or descendant; both source columns must be preserved.
The 273 versus 258 gestation-days first-row figures are source numerical material, not safe or clinically valid fetal term predictions.
The full gestation-distance and month/day numeric tables on PDF536 have not been independently fully transcribed, cross-checked or compared to medical outcomes.
The proposed 13-degree tolerance is broad and source-defined; no sample denominator or error calibration is given.
The method permits benefic/malefic aspects to advance or delay a proposed birth when conception Moon mismatches, adding interpretive flexibility.
The merchant example's Moon near Gemini 1°44, estimated ascendant, gestation distance and approximate 285 days rely on an unverified horoscope and ephemerides.
1616 is divisible by four and a Julian leap year, but year convention and local calendar for source conception days require independent historical checking.
The example calendar arithmetic 244 days through August + 19 Sept = 263; 263+366-285 = 344; 334+10 = Dec10 is internally valid, but its conception date is hypothetical.
The source's proposed 10 December 1615 conception date is not independently documented and does not establish gestation exactly 285 days.
The source reports Moon at noon on proposed conception date about 28°13 Sagittarius, roughly eight degrees from natal ascendant, without astronomical independent re-casting.
A later lunar daily motion about 15°07 is source-provided and may be calendar- and ephemeris-dependent.
The proposed conception clock about 1 AM Sunday night is semantically ambiguous at the midnight boundary and has no pregnancy record.
Lilly says the merchant chart was 'precisely' rectified through accidents and Midheaven/Ascendant directions, but supplies no independent validation of the corrected birth instant in this chapter.
The alternative conception-hour method discussed on PDF539 is explicitly denied any credit by Lilly; it must not be promoted as an endorsed original rule.
The following printed Chapter XCIX Animodar begins on PDF539 with a separate Ptolemaic syzygy/dignity method; its substantive rules are navigation only here.
No independent natal time, human life-event validation, blind comparator, chart parity or runtime prediction promotion is established.
